name: DocVQA
ability_definition: The ability to see details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).

task_realism.reasoning: Reading fine print, handwriting, tables and forms on close-range documents is a common workplace use of near vision. Clerical, legal, medical-records and administrative work all depend on it. However, much workplace near vision involves physical objects: inspecting small parts, circuit boards, gauges, stitching, or specimens. DocVQA does not touch these. Its question-answer framing also emphasizes information retrieval over detecting fine detail.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The standard protocol supplies pre-extracted OCR tokens, and top 2022 systems such as ERNIE-Layout rely on them. The hardest part of the visual acuity problem is therefore often bypassed rather than tested. Other conditions also differ from real work. Images are static, fixed-resolution scans. Detail size and resolution are not systematically varied. There is no need to adjust viewing, zoom, or re-inspect, and there are no time or error stakes.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice of near vision: resolving printed and handwritten text in documents. Success is heavily confounded with layout understanding and reading comprehension rather than determined by acuity alone. It does not measure detecting small marks, thin lines, tiny components, or non-text fine detail, and it offers no graded measure of acuity.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are real scanned industry documents (letters, forms, tables, reports) of the kind workers actually read. Outputs are extracted text answers, which resemble real lookup tasks. However, answers are short spans scored by ANLS rather than full work products, and the OCR-token input channel is an artificial convenience that does not exist in a pure visual task.

transferability_reasoning: DocVQA uses realistic close-range document images and captures the document-reading portion of near vision. Its transfer to the broader ability is weak, though. The supplied OCR tokens let systems sidestep pixel-level acuity, success mixes vision with reading comprehension, and non-text fine-detail inspection is absent. Scores are best read as document understanding with a partial, indirect near-vision signal.

2022.metric: ANLS (Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity) on the DocVQA test set, rescaled from 0–1 to 0–100 (0.8841 on the leaderboard)
2022.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal corrected near vision who read scanned documents such as forms, tables and letters at work (office and clerical workers)
